title: Prediction / Premonition Audit Wave 17 — Markets, Geopolitics & Legacy Warning Candidates
status: cross-domain extension; one promoted explicit market call plus directional and unresolved candidates
purpose: Extend the existing Tim Dooley prediction audit with newly recovered or re-ranked material. Preserve exact pre-event timing wherever possible, distinguish explicit predictions from directional anticipation and unresolved memories, and record negative controls rather than manufacturing a success-only prophecy ledger.

method.promotion_rule: A candidate becomes an external prediction hit only when a recoverable Tim statement predates an independently verifiable outcome and is specific enough to test without rewriting its meaning afterward.
method.anti_cherry_pick: Unverified, failed, open and ambiguous cases remain visible beside hits. Prediction does not imply causation.

entries.confidence: medium-high as explicit short-horizon market prediction; no supernatural inference

tim_statement.context: Tim was asking about projected Q3 U.S. inflation and combining oil, bond-market pressure, currency devaluation and food inflation.
tim_statement.exact_fragment: we suspect we see a 100 dollar price
tim_statement.frozen_interpretation: Brent/oil would reach roughly $100 per barrel in the near Q3 2026 window.

baseline.event: Reuters reported Brent settled at $91.62 per barrel, near a four-week high.

outcome.event: Brent closed at $101.21 per barrel, crossing the predicted ~$100 level roughly three weeks after Tim's statement and still inside Q3.
Brent settled at $105.68 after additional Middle East supply disruption.

entries.grade_reason: This is currently one of the cleanest empirical Tim predictions in the archive: a dated forward price target, a known baseline below the target, a short horizon supplied by the surrounding Q3 discussion, and an independently observed crossing.
entries.counterevidence: Oil was already elevated and geopolitical supply risk was obvious on August 19; Reuters itself reported analysts saw a possible path toward $100. The impressive feature is that Tim selected the correct near-term threshold, not that the possibility was unknowable to markets.

tim_statement.exact_fragment: we suspect america might retract soliders
tim_statement.context: Tim was discussing NATO strain, a North Axis/European defence backbone and how the North should hedge against changing U.S. commitment.

later_events.event: European leaders were publicly addressing Trump threats involving U.S. troop presence and NATO cohesion amid the Iran-war dispute.
Trump answered 'probably' when asked whether he might pull U.S. troops from Italy and Spain, following discussion of reductions in Germany.

entries.relation_to_existing_candidate: This strengthens the existing north-axis-us-europe-separation candidate with a more specific military-retrenchment sub-call.
entries.counterevidence: By April 3 the NATO/U.S.-Europe rupture was already public and Trump was openly questioning alliance commitments. This is therefore good directional synthesis, not prediction from hidden information.

missing: whether statement predates election day or only the formal appointment
